title: Hyperpigmentation on Cheeks: Causes, Care and When to See a Doctor
ex: Why cheeks darken so easily, how to tell acne marks, tan and melasma apart, a gentle sunscreen-first routine, and when to see a dermatologist.
rt: Hyperpigmentation on Cheeks: Causes & Care | Mirc Glow
rd: Hyperpigmentation on cheeks: common causes, how to spot possible melasma, a gentle sunscreen-first routine, helpful ingredients and realistic timelines.
quick: Hyperpigmentation on cheeks usually comes from sun and heat, acne marks, friction or hormones. Daily sunscreen, gentle cleansing and a night cream with niacinamide, kojic acid or alpha arbutin help patches look more even over 8–12 weeks. Symmetrical patches linked to hormones may be melasma: see a dermatologist.
facts: The cheekbones are among the most sun-exposed parts of the face.
Melasma often shows as symmetrical patches on both cheeks.
Scrubs and lemon can make patches look darker.
